the_result: +10 points of localisation, +1 episode at most. G-trivial′ — the model's OWN hypothesis text at the same forced region — lands exactly on the baseline. The v1 conclusion reproduces on a task set built to be different.

divergence_check_baseline_vs_gtrivial_pr.reading: the arms are two runs, not one: the 8 changed first hypotheses are exactly the +10 localisation points, and 58 trajectories diverge later because the selected candidate's `why` text differs even when region and class match, which changes the history string. Route changes, destination does not — the same signature as v1.

what_it_leaves: on the ORIGINAL loop, v2 behaves like v1 on this axis. That is consistent with the structural finding that the step-1 decision carries no observation: 80 episodes, six distinct prompts. Both controls are therefore measuring a choice made blind, which is why 改善 in localisation does not convert. The inspect-first loop (理 10941) is the test of whether a choice made WITH an observation behaves differently.
bounds: 80 episodes, four slices, greedy. The +1 is noise.
G-trivial is handed task['bug_class'], the TRUE class, so it is an oracle on the class as well as the region. G-trivial′ must invent the class and still matches the baseline.
These are ORIGINAL-loop numbers. 理 ruled everything on v2 re-runs under inspect-first and is compared only within that loop; this set is the before, kept for the contrast.
